meta.title: Custom Software and ERP Integration
meta.description: Genixo builds internal systems, ERP and e-invoice integrations, field apps and reporting around how your company works, starting with a discovery sprint.

hero.title: Software that fits how you work and talks to the systems you have
hero.lead: When orders live in WhatsApp, prices in Excel and invoices in the ERP, the problem is rarely your team. We connect the pieces, or build the missing one.

answer.label: In short
answer.text: Genixo builds custom internal systems and integrations for SMEs and organizations: ERP, CRM and e-invoice connections, field apps, reporting from a single source and step-by-step modernization of existing systems. Work starts with a discovery sprint that produces the scope, the architecture and a fixed quote.

sections.label: Sound familiar?
sections.title: Signs that your tools no longer fit
items: The same order is entered three times: in the sales sheet, the ERP and the warehouse list.
The monthly report takes days because the numbers come from four places that don't agree.
Our field team works on paper or WhatsApp because the app doesn't work without signal.
The old system runs the business, but nobody dares to touch it.
We bought a package, then paid to bend our processes around it.

items.title: Internal systems
items.text: Order, stock, dispatch, service or approval workflows built around the way your teams already work.

items.title: ERP, CRM and e-invoice integrations
items.text: Your existing systems exchange data automatically, so nobody copies numbers from one screen to another.

items.title: Field apps for weak connections
items.text: Mobile apps that keep working offline and sync when the connection returns.

items.title: Reporting from one source
items.text: Dashboards and reports that read from one consistent data source, so management sees one version of the numbers.

items.title: Modernization without a big-bang switch
items.text: Old systems replaced piece by piece, with the old and new running side by side until the switch is safe.

items.title: Cost review before cost promises
items.text: We look at where time and licence money actually go before suggesting what to build. We don't promise savings we haven't measured.

items.title: Discovery sprint
items.text: We map the process and the systems involved. Output: scope, architecture and a fixed quote.

items.title: Build in increments
items.text: You see working software every week and adjust priorities with us as it takes shape.

items.title: Launch
items.text: Data migration, user training and a switch-over planned with the people who use the system.

items.title: Improve
items.text: After go-live we fix, extend and measure, as a separate phase or through NGSD.

sections.label: Why it matters for AI
sections.title: Clean data from today's system is what AI needs tomorrow
paragraphs: AI automation works on structured, reliable data. When orders, deliveries and invoices are captured in one system with consistent fields, later steps such as order matching or demand forecasting become possible.
That is why many AI projects start as software projects. See [AI process automation](/ai-automation) for what comes next.

sections.label: What stays in your control
sections.title: Ownership and continuity
items: Source code, documentation and infrastructure access are handed over to you. [[TODO-028]]
We use widely known technologies, such as Spring Boot, Next.js, PostgreSQL and Docker, so another team can maintain the system later.
If you decide to move the work in-house, we hand over the code and what we know about it. [[TODO-029]]

sections.label: What this is not
sections.title: Limits
items: We don't replace a working package just to build something new. If configuration solves the problem, we say so.
We don't quote a fixed price before the discovery sprint has defined the scope.
We don't take on more projects than our team can staff properly.

items.q: Is custom software more expensive than a package?
items.a: At the start, usually yes. The comparison that matters includes licence fees, the cost of working around a poor fit and the manual work between systems. The discovery sprint gives you a fixed quote so you can compare.

items.q: Can you integrate with our ERP?
items.a: In most cases, yes, through the ERP's API, database views or file exchange. During discovery we confirm which integration methods your ERP version supports.

items.q: Can you take over an existing system built by someone else?
items.a: Often, yes. We start by reviewing the code, the infrastructure and the documentation, then tell you what can be kept and what is risky.
